title: Characterisation of multiplication inputs
statement: For bit strings $a,b,c$, the nested encoding $\langle a,\langle b,c\rangle\rangle$ belongs to the language of binary multiplication exactly when $a,b,c$ are canonical, $|c|\le |a|+|b|$, the carry after column $|a|+|b|$ is zero, and for every $j<|a|+|b|$, the $j$th bit of $c$ equals the remainder modulo $2$ of the sum of the carry into column $j$ and the product-column value at $j$.
hypotheses_covered: Membership of the nested encoding in the multiplication language is equivalent to all listed conditions
The carry at column $|a|+|b|$ is zero
For every $j<|a|+|b|$, the stated bit-and-column equation holds
